name: Ecwid
description: Ecommerce: embeddable SaaS shopping-cart platform (Ecwid by Lightspeed) with a REST API for products, orders, customers, discounts and storefront settings.
access_notes: REST API is only available on paid plans (Venture, Business, Unlimited); Free-plan stores cannot use the API at all. For your own store, a custom app with static public/secret access tokens is auto-created in the admin app dashboard (used as Bearer tokens, no OAuth flow needed). Public/App-Market apps use OAuth2 authorization code (POST my.ecwid.com/api/oauth/token) yielding non-expiring bearer tokens. Ecwid offers free paid-plan upgrades to App Market developers on request.
mcp_notes: No official Ecwid MCP server found in docs.ecwid.com or Ecwid announcements; no Composio Ecwid toolkit (composio.dev/toolkits/ecwid and docs.composio.dev/toolkits/ecwid return 404).
uncertainty_notes: Webhook setup for an app requires submitting the webhookUrl and event list to Ecwid via an application-update request (app settings are read-only for developers), which adds a manual step. Searches tried: 'Ecwid MCP server official', Composio toolkit URL probes.

evidence.note: OAuth 2.0 for public apps; for your own store, copy the custom app's secret token from the app dashboard and use it as a Bearer token.
OAuth2 authorization_code exchange at POST my.ecwid.com/api/oauth/token/{store_id}; token_type is always bearer.
'Only stores on paid plans can access API'; free paid-plan upgrades available for developers on request.
REST API manages 'any store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings'; 600 req/min per token rate limit.
Webhooks are real-time POST notifications to a self-hosted webhookUrl, signed with X-Ecwid-Webhook-Signature (HMAC SHA-256).
